answer: The ember log keeps the sampled set and the penalty so the deterrent is verifiable. Because selection is random and the tundra seed is unrevealed until close, someone cannot dodge the sample, so colluding to grade clones' junk is a dune gamble with a negative expected value. A random sample of settled verdicts is re-graded by an independent panel each epoch, and a divergence found on re-check costs the original grader 15% of its standing plus a seat ban. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
